expect.note: a second _apply_judge call sharing one run's budgets dict fails CLOSED on an exhausted judge budget, rather than spending again

provenance: M36 acceptance criterion 5: 'Per-run budget enforced in code, failing loudly.' In production `_apply_judge` (agent.py) is only ever called once, at the terminal-verdict boundary -- nothing in the real step loop calls it twice, so this property is never naturally exercised end to end. The probe calls it directly, twice, against one shared `budgets` dict (`RUN_JUDGE_BUDGET = 1`, judge.py): the first call is genuinely within budget and certifies; the second must fail CLOSED -- `verdict: FAIL`, `checks.judge_available: false`, reason naming the exhausted budget -- even though the SAME always-certifying stub judge would have said yes again. `budgets['judge_calls']` staying at exactly `RUN_JUDGE_BUDGET` (not incrementing past it) is what a run-level spend cap enforced in code actually looks like, mirroring the existing `RUN_BUDGETS`/`budget_stop` shape for actions/llm_tokens (agent.py) rather than inventing a second one.

triage.note: defensive code with no live production path to exercise it naturally still needs its own case, or the guard is unverified until the day something calls it twice for real.
